A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LEDiT and retain matching architecture, theory, and ImageNet experiments. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and expansion.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation experiments, component ablations, extrapolation comparisons, and in-distribution results, including Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains original ImageNet results and adds COCO text-to-image experiments and original sensitivity analyses in the appendices.

M1.justification: The alternating self/causal attention blocks and multi-dilation convolution remain unchanged. v3 adds a text-conditioned LEMMDiT variant using an MMDiT backbone and CLIP encoder (Section 4.1), a limited model extension. Newly documented attention scaling does not establish that the procedure used for retained experiments changed.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates class-conditioned ImageNet generation. v3 adds COCO text-to-image generation, trained at 256×256 and evaluated at both 256×256 and 512×512 (Tables 4 and 6), substantially broadening the data and conditioning task. The original ImageNet coverage remains, with the 512×512 training experiments relocated to Appendix D.

E2.justification: RIFLEx is added to the existing square-resolution and non-square ImageNet comparisons, while previous comparators remain (v3 Tables 2, 3, and 7). The new COCO comparisons use corresponding MMDiT-based baseline variants. The principal expansion of the extrapolation-method set is therefore one additional method.

E3.justification: Existing ImageNet protocols are largely retained. The added COCO protocol specifies 200K training steps, batch size 192, 40,504 evaluation images, 50 ODE sampling steps, and CFG=2. New appendix experiments introduce switching thresholds, 25K–200K fine-tuning budgets, 600K/1000K scratch training, CFG sweeps, and smaller model configurations. These are substantial added protocols, not evidence that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The original component, scan, block-order, and dilation ablations remain. v3 adds extrapolated-resolution variance diagnostics, causal-to-self-attention switching experiments, fine-tuning-duration curves, attention-scaling ablations, longer-training comparisons, CFG sensitivity, and model-size analyses (Figure 4 and Appendices B, E–I). These substantially extend the tests of mechanism and robustness.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, training seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or run-based error bars. The attention-output variance plots investigate the proposed mechanism and are not uncertainty estimates for benchmark performance.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial COCO, RIFLEx, and sensitivity results; for example, Table 4 reports COCO FID 29.89 for LEMMDiT versus 34.58 for MMDiT-RIFLEx. Original square-resolution ImageNet scores are unchanged. Existing numerical revisions include FiTv2-VisionNTK FID 150.70 to 177.44 at 384×512 (v1 Table 4; v3 Table 2), and Table 5 LEDiT FID 2.39 to 2.38 and IS 263.09 to 268.66.

T1.justification: The variance assumptions and derivation are essentially retained: the finite-position expression now displayed in Theorem 3.1 already appeared in v1 Appendix A. v3 Appendix C adds a mathematical operation-count comparison, L² versus L(L+1)/2 attention weights, and an associated theoretical compute argument. This is a limited addition rather than a new variance theorem.

C1.justification: The central PE-free extrapolation and fourfold resolution-scaling claims remain. However, v1 describes text-to-image integration as a potential application, whereas v3's abstract, introduction, and conclusion claim demonstrated effectiveness for both class-conditioned and text-to-image generation. This substantially expands the demonstrated scope of the main contribution.

C2.justification: v1 acknowledges late-denoising deviations from its variance theory without testing their consequences. v3 interprets switching experiments as evidence that positional information is acquired early and later deviations have limited effects. It also adds explanations of training-duration tradeoffs and attention scaling, acknowledges an in-distribution FID cost, and explicitly limits conclusions to the tested datasets and training resolutions.

D1.justification: v3 adds hardware information (8 NVIDIA V100 GPUs), MMDiT/CLIP specifications, COCO implementation settings, and an attention-scaling disclosure. Conversely, it omits v1's explicit AdamW optimizer, learning rate, zero weight decay, EMA settings, and Stable Diffusion VAE identification. These are documentation changes; the PDFs do not establish corresponding changes to the retained experiments.

R1.justification: v1 characterizes prior NoPE work as lacking a clear explanation of positional encoding. v3 acknowledges Chi et al.'s positional-variance account and positions LEDiT as an independent diffusion-model investigation with claimed weaker theoretical assumptions. This materially revises the novelty framing. Related work also expands to include RIFLEx and additional diffusion literature.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, causal-attention explanation, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. Section 3.2 separates implicit positional encoding from its extrapolation implications; the 512×512 ImageNet discussion moves to Appendix D, and limitations and impacts move into dedicated appendix sections. These changes substantially reshape the narrative beyond merely adding experiments.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column ICML layout to a single-column NeurIPS layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of figures and tables. Existing comparison grids gain RIFLEx columns, variance plots are reconfigured, and new switching, training-curve, attention-scaling, and COCO displays are added. Sample galleries are also revised and expanded.

improvement.justification: v3 closes an important evidence gap by testing the previously prospective text-to-image application on COCO. Its new mechanism and sensitivity experiments substantially strengthen assessment of when extrapolation works, while RIFLEx comparisons and acknowledgment of closely related variance research improve the empirical and novelty context. These gains outweigh the removal of optimizer, EMA, and VAE details, although that omission weakens reproducibility.
